next_steps: Redwood to share updated network diagram and peering guide
Customer to run 24h perf run on staging with new kernel; share logs
Schedule on-prem upgrade window week of 2025-04-28
action_items: Anna: Send updated network diagram + peering checklist (due: 2025-04-18)
Javier: Provide kernel/quantization config used in last run + perf dashboard links (due: 2025-04-18)

summary: Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Reviewed networking/peering progress, on-prem package upgrade schedule, recent perf runs and tuning steps. Identified a networking egress issue causing intermittent failures; agreed next steps to run 24h perf on staging with updated kernel and to schedule an on-prem upgrade window. Action items assigned and follow-up meeting scheduled.
transcript:
[00:00] Anna (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'll kick off — this is the weekly sync for the private vpc pilot. quick roll call?
[00:08] Mark (BrightHealth): Mark here, hi.
[00:11] Sana (Customer): Sana — ML.
[00:13] Tom (CTO): Tom on.
[00:15] Lauren (Security): Lauren here.
[00:17] Javier (Redwood SE): Javier here. good morning all.
[00:20] Anna: ok, quick agenda — networking/peering updates, perf run results, on-prem upgrade plan, security questions and then next steps. any additions?
[00:28] Mark: nope, that's it.
[00:30] Anna: great. Javier can you walk through the peering status?
[00:34] Javier: yeah, sure. so as of this morning we have the peering connection provisioned but we saw intermittent egress blocks from the customer VPC to the redwood bastion. looks like a firewall rule missing on the cloud side, not on our end. we saw about 6 failed attempts in the 02:00–03:00 UTC window where the handshake dropped.
[00:55] Mark: yeah that was me — sorry, we were tightening outbound rules after an incident, i missed the entry to allow the redwood egress ip range.
[01:02] Anna: ok, good catch. what's the plan to remediate?
[01:05] Mark: i'll open a ticket with cloud infra to add the rule and run a connectivity check. will also add an allow-list for the whole redwood range so we don't have to tweak per ip.
[01:15] Javier: once that's in place we recommend doing a 24 hour perf run on staging to exercise long-tail behaviors — prefix caching, kv cash hotpaths, and to look for reconnects. our last run saw 1.8% reconnects under bursty traffic.
[01:35] Sana: 1.8% reconnects — does that materially affect latency percentiles?
[01:39] Javier: it bumped p99 by ~120ms in that window. average latency held steady though. remember we also had a quant config change which reduced token cost but may have slightly increased tail latency.
[01:50] Anna: quick reminder, the quantization profile we used was q4_0-fast (or something) — the seq len in your tests was 512 typical, that matters for kernel choice.
[02:03] Tom: on the on-prem upgrade — what's the dependency list? are there required kernel modules? we want to schedule downtime.
[02:11] Javier: yes, the new runtime requires the 6.1+ kernel for some of the fused attention paths; we also ship a set of optimized cuda kernels. for on-prem the typical steps: pre-check script, stop services, apply package, run migrations, then smoke tests and bring up canary. downtime estimate ~45 minutes but we'll plan 2 hours for safety.
[02:34] Mark: that's fine. what's the rollback story?
[02:37] Javier: we keep the previous container images and a config-based toggle for the kernel selection; rollback is usually re-deploy previous images and restore kv cache warmup script — we recommend keeping prefixes warmed for 30 minutes after rollback.
[02:50] Lauren: on security — i'll need the install steps and the list of ports + cert rotation process; also confirm we can integrate with our KMS/HSM.
[02:59] Anna: yes, we'll share the installer guide and KMS integration notes. we support customer-managed KMS for private; HSM is available via our enterprise package.
[03:09] Lauren: any audit logs available? we need end-to-end tracing for data access.
[03:13] Priya (CSM): we can confirm audit logs are available for private deployments; retention configurable. we'll include sample schema in the doc bundle.
[03:21] Tom: re: latency vs cost — can you remind us of the knobs? we want to hit p95 < 200ms for inference while keeping unit costs reasonable.
[03:29] Javier: main levers: batch size, kv prefix caching, quant profile, and instance type. we recommended steady-state batching of 8 for your workload, which keeps p95 ~180ms on our staging profiles. switching to q4_1 reduced cost by ~20% but increased p99 slightly — tradeoff as always.
[03:51] Sana: when you say 'kv prefix caching' are you referring to the prefix cache at the serving runtime or something in our app?
[03:56] Javier: serving runtime — automatic prefix cache that stores KV caches for frequent prompts. it's conservative in eviction but you can configure TTLs. in one of the runs we saw the cache miss rate jump when you had long-tail prefixes which explains some token spend variance.
[04:12] Anna: quick note — the transcript may show kv "cash" sometimes; auto-transcript.
[04:17] Mark: ha, fair.
[04:20] Anna: ok, lets look at last week's perf summary. Javier, you patched the kernel-level scheduling; what changed?
[04:25] Javier: we enabled a new fusion kernel for attention and bumped the kv cache prefetch thresholds — that reduced CPU jitter and decreased per-token wall time by ~6% median. attached dashboard link in the notes, but highlights: median latency 95ms, p95 178ms, p99 360ms, token cost down 12%.
[04:49] Sana: the p99 360ms still seems high for some tails — is that mostly reconnects? or sequence length variance?
[04:55] Javier: mix of both. reconnect spikes accounted for roughly 40% of those tails in the window we looked at; the rest were long sequences >1024 and a few outlier requests that triggered recompile.
[05:08] Anna: recompile meaning kernel re-selection at runtime?
[05:11] Javier: yep, when seq len crosses threshold sometimes runtime chooses a different kernel and there's a short penalty. we're working on warm-start heuristics to pre-select based on recent seq len histogram.
[05:22] Tom: cool. any blockers on the on-prem package?
[05:25] Javier: one note — the installer currently requires outbound access to redwood update endpoints to fetch optimized kernels during install. for air-gapped installs we provide an offline bundle but we'll need to coordinate delivery and checksums.
[05:39] Mark: we're not air-gapped, but egress must go through our proxy. do you have curl-friendly endpoints or a small artifact we can host internally?
[05:46] Anna: yes, we can provide both options — an s3-friendly artifact list + checksums and direct endpoints. Javier will send the bundle reference.
[05:54] Javier: i'll include an md5/sha256 list and the small installer tar. for your proxy we documented expected hostnames in the install guide.
[06:03] Lauren: what's the timeline for the kernel changes making it into the GA on-prem build?
[06:07] Javier: next build scheduled for 2025-04-28; we're running integration tests now. if tests pass we'll open the release candidate on 04-25 for you to test in staging.
[06:18] Mark: can we get a changelog with the exact kernel reqs and package sizes?
[06:22] Anna: yes — will be in the doc bundle.
[06:24] Priya: also we'll include a pre-check script you can run to verify prerequisites before the upgrade window.
[06:30] Sana: re: perf testing — what's the recommended workload generator? we used locust but want to make sure it's exercising kv cache correctly.
[06:36] Javier: we recommend our benchmark harness (link in notes). it simulates prompt reuse patterns and caches. if you prefer locust we have a plugin that reproduces prefix reuse. i'll share both.
[06:45] Mark: about the intermittent failed requests — any logs you can share to help debug?
[06:49] Javier: yes, we captured connection traces and agent logs for the failing windows; i'll upload sanitized logs to the shared folder.
[06:56] Anna: okay next — billing/commits? any updates from procurement?
[07:00] Tom: procurement is reviewing the dedicated vs private license terms. we still need to confirm data residency requirements before signing.
[07:07] Anna: under understand. top-level for private we support region pinning; we can include data residency clauses in the SOW.
[07:14] Lauren: also need SSO and RBAC details for initial rollout — do you support SCIM?
[07:19] Priya: yes, scim and sso via SAML and OIDC are supported; we can share the SSO config steps.
[07:26] Mark: one small oddity — in staging we saw token accounting mismatch vs what our internal meter reports. about 3% difference. any known causes?
[07:34] Javier: possible reasons: your client-side batched requests maybe accounting differently for system tokens; also retried requests double-count if retries hit different endpoints. we'll compare logs.
[07:44] Anna: ok let's capture a sample trace of a request with accounting metadata and we'll reconcile. action item for Javier + Mark.
[07:52] Javier: noted.
[07:54] Anna: anything else on the technical side?
[07:56] Tom: one last ask — can we run a canary with 20% traffic to dedicated nodes for a week to see tail behavior in our production-like traffic?
[08:06] Javier: yes that's doable. we'd provision dedicated capacity and route 20% via smart routing; we'd need an SSO token and routing rule from you and a date window.
[08:15] Anna: we'll prepare the plan and send a routing template; mark will confirm the start date.
[08:21] Mark: sounds good.
[08:23] Anna: ok let's recap next steps — javier to send kernel + quant configs, network diagram and installer bundle; mark to add firewall rule and run staging 24h; lauren to send security questions; anna to share peering checklist and follow-up meeting invite.
[08:40] Priya: i'll add those to the ticket and send calendar invite for the follow up — same time next week.
[08:47] Tom: perfect. thanks everyone.
[08:50] Anna: thanks all, end of call.
duration_transcript_alignment_note: Transcript timestamps approximate; call lasted ~45 minutes per meeting record. Some auto-transcript mistakes (kv cash, casing of product names) present.
